description: Policy input for tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-vpn-tor.sh, nuxel-privacyd and the Privacy control centre PWA. Nothing here is applied by itself: this file is read, the tool acts, and the tool prints the evidence of what it did.

target.console_interface: usb0 (CDC-ACM/RNDIS gadget) - the only recovery path; never used for app egress

rules: A claim is 'evidenced' ONLY with the command output that proves it, quoted next to the claim.
traffic_routed_through_tor and traffic_routed_through_vpn are 'unproven' by default and stay unproven until an external-vantage leak test passes; the device cannot prove them alone.
killswitch_armed NEVER implies tunnel_interface_up: they are reported separately, always.
unknown is a valid answer. No claim is ever upgraded to make a UI look better.

wireguard.note: The private key is referenced by path and never stored in this repository or in the status output.

networkmanager.note: Used when nmcli is present; the tool reports which backend it actually used.

dns.note: DNS must be resolved inside the tunnel (resolv.conf pointed at the tunnel's resolver or at 127.0.0.1 for Tor). A plaintext DNS query while a tunnel is up is reported as a LEAK-SUSPECT, not hidden.

bridges.note: Bridge lines are intentionally absent: this repository ships no bridge addresses and no pluggable-transport binaries. In a censored network the owner adds them at /etc/tor/bridges.conf and reruns 'nuxel-vpn-tor.sh tor bridges-apply'. Until then the tool reports bridges as unconfigured instead of pretending to defeat censorship.

leak_probe.note: The probe counts plaintext DNS (udp/tcp 53) and direct outbound connections from the probe process while forcing a name resolution. It is a device-side smoke test, NOT proof of anonymisation: an external vantage point is required for that, and the tool says so in the verdict.

remote_access.note: Remote access must be off by default and must show a visible indicator while enabled; the indicator state is written by the CLI and read by the PWA.

daemon.name: nuxel-privacyd
daemon.honest_note: The daemon serves STATUS read-only to any local process and refuses state changes unless the caller presents the root token (a 0600 root-owned file an unprivileged app cannot read). The control-centre PWA therefore queues a request and shows the exact console command; it never silently escalates.
